name: Belur Math
description: Headquarters of Ramakrishna Mission on the Hooghly. Built in a style combining Hindu, Islamic, and Christian architecture.

name: Birla Planetarium
description: Second-largest planetarium in Asia. Daily shows on astronomy, cosmology, and space exploration.

name: College Street Book Market
description: World's largest secondhand book market. Miles of bookstalls with the famous Indian Coffee House.

name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
description: Temple where Ramakrishna Paramahamsa had his spiritual visions. 12 Shiva temples in the compound.

name: Eden Gardens
description: Iconic cricket stadium — oldest and one of largest in the world. 66,000 capacity. Museum inside.

name: Howrah Bridge
description: Iconic cantilever bridge over the Hooghly River. One of the busiest bridges in the world with no nuts or bolts.

name: Indian Museum
description: Oldest and largest museum in India (1814). Egyptian mummy, Gandhara sculptures, and meteorite collection.

name: Jorasanko Thakur Bari (Tagore House)
description: Ancestral home of Rabindranath Tagore where he was born and died. Museum of his life, art, and manuscripts.

name: Kalighat Kali Temple
description: One of 51 Shakti Peethas. Ancient temple where the city of Calcutta derives its name from.

name: Kumartuli (Potters' Quarter)
description: Artisan quarter where clay idols for Durga Puja and other festivals are sculpted. Living craft heritage.

name: Marble Palace
description: Neoclassical mansion with art collection including Rubens, Reynolds, and Titian paintings. Free entry.

name: Mother House (Mother Teresa's Home)
description: Headquarters of Missionaries of Charity. Mother Teresa's tomb and small museum of her life.

name: Mullick Ghat Flower Market
description: Largest flower market in Asia below Howrah Bridge. 2,000+ vendors. Best visited at dawn.

name: Prinsep Ghat
description: Neoclassical colonnade on the Hooghly riverbank. Sunset views and evening boat rides.

name: South Park Street Cemetery
description: Gothic colonial cemetery from 1767 with ornate tombs. One of the oldest non-church cemeteries in the world.

name: St. Paul's Cathedral
description: Gothic Revival cathedral built 1839-1847. Stained glass windows, frescoes, and colonial-era architecture.

name: Victoria Memorial
description: Magnificent white marble hall built 1906-1921. Museum of British-era paintings, manuscripts, and artifacts.

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Venue of the famous Hornbill Festival (Dec 1-10). Naga tribal morungs, bamboo architecture, and cultural showcases.

name: Kohima Cathedral
description: One of the largest cathedrals in Asia. Center of Nagaland's predominantly Christian community.

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery. Marks the site of the Battle of Kohima (1944) — turning point of WWII in Asia.

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: Artifacts, weapons, textiles, and ceremonial objects of all 16 Naga tribes. Tribal heritage showcase.

name: Barot Trout Farm
description: Government fish farm breeding rainbow and brown trout. Surrounded by mountains with fishing opportunities.

name: Nargu Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Dense forest sanctuary home to Himalayan black bear, monal, and leopard. Great for birding.

name: Shanan Hydroelectric Project
description: Asia's first hydro project built by Col. Ninon in 1932. British-era marvel of engineering.

name: Jalori Pass
description: Mountain pass at 10,282 ft with panoramic Himalayan views. Starting point for Serolsar Lake trek.

name: Jibhi Waterfall
description: Hidden waterfall reached via a short forest trail. Crystal-clear pool at the base for wading.

name: Raghupur Fort Trek
description: Ruins of a 14th-century fort perched on a ridge above Jalori Pass with 360-degree mountain views.

name: Birthi Falls
description: 126-meter waterfall on the way to Munsiyari. Short trek from the road to the base.

name: Nanda Devi Base Camp View
description: Panoramic viewpoint of five Panch Chuli peaks glowing at sunrise. One of the best Himalayan panoramas.

name: Tribal Heritage Museum
description: Private museum showcasing artifacts and lifestyle of the Bhotia and Johari tribal communities.

name: EME Temple
description: Unique aluminium-covered temple built by the Indian Army's EME corps. All faiths represented inside.

name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
description: 4x the size of Buckingham Palace. Indo-Saracenic marvel with Italian marble, Belgian stained glass, and Venetian mosaics.

name: Sayaji Baug (Kamati Baug)
description: Sprawling garden with Baroda Museum, planetarium, zoo, toy train, and health museum. All-day family destination.

name: Chandra Taal Lake
description: The crescent moon lake itself, 1km diameter at 4,270m. Walk around the full perimeter takes 30-40 minutes. Camping is banned within 1km of the shore — camps are at Batal/Parasol area.

name: Samudri Tapu Glacier viewpoint
description: The glacier feeding Chandra Taal — visible on the trek from Batal. Source of the Chandra River. Requires acclimatisation; not for day visitors.

name: Goecha La Trek
description: Iconic 10-day trek to Goecha La pass at 15,100 ft. Face-to-face with Kanchenjunga and surrounding 7,000m peaks.

name: Kanchenjunga Base Camp Trail
description: UNESCO World Heritage mixed site. Trek through rhododendron forests to views of the world's 3rd highest peak.

name: Mechuka Valley Walk
description: Flat valley floor walk through Memba tribal villages with Siyom River and snow peaks.

name: Samten Yongcha Monastery
description: Ancient Gelug Buddhist monastery at the edge of the McMahon Line. Peaceful with mountain backdrop.

name: Ranthambore Fort
description: UNESCO World Heritage hill fort within the national park. Ancient temples and dramatic cliff-top views.

name: Ranthambore Tiger Safari
description: One of the best places in India to spot Bengal tigers in the wild. Jeep and canter safaris.

name: Nehru Institute of Mountaineering
description: Premier mountaineering training institute with a museum of expedition artifacts and Everest memorabilia.

name: Vishwanath Temple
description: Ancient Shiva temple with a massive trident (trishul). Believed to be built during the Mahabharata era.

name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
description: One of five Sikh Takhts. Where Guru Gobind Singh compiled the final version of Sri Guru Granth Sahib.

name: Thanamir Village & Saramati Base
description: Small village at base of Saramati Peak. Last supply point before trek. Local homestays and guides available.

name: Glory Peak
description: Highest inhabited town in Nagaland at 7,250 ft. Views of the Dzukou Valley and Manipur hills.

name: Verinag Spring
description: Mughal-era octagonal stone basin at the source of Jhelum River. Built by Emperor Jahangir in 1620.
